clue.text: Glass vessel

definitions.meaning: a tall drinking glass for sherry or beer goes by this name
a sailing ship with fore-and-aft rig on two or more masts

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a large beer or sherry glass and a type of sailing ship.

clue.text: Ought to have some hesitation appearing in this joint

parts.note: should means ought to
er is the sound of a hesitation

explanation.surface: Someone ought to hesitate before showing off this part of the body.
explanation.definitionFit: The ball-and-socket articulation where the arm meets the trunk.

clue.text: No, this ale would be spoiled by a piece of ice

indicators.note: spoiled says these letters are ruined and remade in a new order

explanation.surface: A protest that this beer would be ruined by an ice cube.
explanation.definitionFit: A pellet of frozen rain falling from a storm cloud.

clue.text: Chose a workman?

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
Ted is a man's name

explanation.surface: Picked out a labourer?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark invites splitting 'workman' into two words, 'work' and 'man', each with its own synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Made a choice between alternatives, picked.

clue.text: Mature Republican can make a mistake

indicators.note: can make says the letters can be reworked into something new

explanation.surface: An older Republican politician is capable of an error.
explanation.definitionFit: An error in printing or writing, often listed on a correction slip.

clue.text: Sailor girl in charge of 8?

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is the usual crossword sailor
Bess is a girl's name, short for Elizabeth

explanation.surface: A sailor's girlfriend seems to be running a team of nurses.
explanation.walkthrough: 8 refers to the answer at 8-down, SISTER: a nun who heads a convent is in charge of the sisters. The question mark flags the cross-reference definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of a convent of nuns presides over the community of religious sisters.

clue.text: It stops one seeing the concealed church

parts.note: a blind corner or turning is a concealed one
the fold is the flock of a church, its congregation

explanation.surface: Something prevents a person from seeing the hidden chapel.
explanation.walkthrough: The fold is the Christian flock, so it stands for the church.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloth tied over the eyes to prevent sight.

clue.text: Correct myself at last

indicators.note: at places one word in the midst of the other here

parts.note: the end is the last of something
me means myself

explanation.surface: Fix myself in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at' signals putting one word into the other: myself sits inside the last.
explanation.definitionFit: To revise or put right a text by removing its errors.

clue.text: She tends to resist change

indicators.note: change tells us the word resist is rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman inclined to oppose any reform.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior hospital nurse looks after patients on a ward.

clue.text: Revolutionary may take a whip-round to gain prestige

indicators.note: round puts the lash around the revolutionary

parts.note: the cat-o'-nine-tails is a whip, known as the cat
Che Guevara is the usual crossword revolutionary

explanation.surface: A rebel might hold a collection to win standing.
explanation.definitionFit: Distinction or status that commands respect.

clue.text: In part of the Gobi, it died

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone perished in a stretch of the Asian desert.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for 'he or she died', used on gravestones and in obituary records.

clue.text: Study one head's maturity

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it at university
I is the Roman numeral for one
a ness is a headland, a head of land jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: Learning and one person's leadership show how grown-up they are.
explanation.definitionFit: Being fully ripe or developed means being prepared, a state of preparedness.

clue.text: Endure long depression in the ultimate resort

parts.note: to last is to endure or go on
a ditch is a long trench dug in the ground

explanation.surface: Putting up with a lengthy slump when all else has failed.
explanation.definitionFit: A final stand made when every other option is gone, a desperate final effort.

clue.text: Avoid this city

definitions.meaning: ... City is a town in Kansas famed from Wild West stories

explanation.definitionFit: To evade is a synonym; Dodge City in Kansas is the Wild West town of that name.

clue.text: Self-centredness of Cockney — he irritated his master

indicators.note: a Cockney, a working-class Londoner, drops the aitch from words like he and his

parts.note: got, as in 'it got to me', means irritated
M is an abbreviation for master, as in MA

explanation.surface: A Londoner's selfishness annoyed his employer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cockney' acts on both he and his, since East Londoners traditionally drop the aitch at the start of words.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessive preoccupation with oneself and one's own importance is vanity of the ego.

clue.text: Not having been willing to order satinette

indicators.note: to order means the fabric's letters are put into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Unwilling to place an order for a satin-like fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not having been willing' puns on making a will: someone who dies without one.
explanation.definitionFit: Dying without having made a will to leave one's estate.

clue.text: Small digger with spiked wheel on end of shaft

indicators.note: on places the spur wheel after the letter it rests upon in the across entry
end of picks the closing letter of the word shaft

parts.note: a rowel is the small spiked wheel on a rider's spur

explanation.surface: A tiny excavator fitted with a spiked wheel at the far end of its axle.
explanation.definitionFit: A gardener's hand tool used for scooping and digging small holes.

clue.text: Letter writer is always poetical about Falstaff's companion

indicators.note: about makes the poetic word surround the companion

parts.note: e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, meaning always
Pistol is one of Falstaff's cronies in Shakespeare

explanation.surface: A correspondent is forever writing verse about one of Falstaff's crew.
explanation.definitionFit: One who reads the Epistle in church, or a writer of epistles, letters.

clue.text: Ask 'to become a Quaker to gain favour

parts.note: to be is to become, exist as
Quakers are members of the Religious Society of Friends

explanation.surface: Someone is invited to join the Quakers to win approval.
explanation.walkthrough: Quakers call themselves Friends, so 'to become a Quaker' is to BE FRIEND.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a friend of someone and win their goodwill.

clue.text: Collar this girl

definitions.meaning: a wide deep collar on a woman's dress

explanation.definitionFit: A wide lace neckpiece on a dress shares its name with a woman's first name.

clue.text: Indian thug in Paris

definitions.meaning: a Native American people of the US Southwest
in French slang a Parisian street ruffian

explanation.definitionFit: A Native American people and the French slang word for a street ruffian.

clue.text: There are laws about one German analgesic

parts.note: a code is a body of laws

indicators.note: about signals that the German word is turned around and rearranged

parts.note: ein is German for one

explanation.surface: Germany has regulations covering a certain painkiller.
explanation.definitionFit: An opiate drug derived from morphine, taken to relieve pain.

clue.text: Halfway through the dance, bare one's teeth in annoyance

indicators.note: halfway through takes the first half of the dance's name

parts.note: the cha-cha is a Latin ballroom dance
to grin is to show one's teeth

explanation.surface: Midway through the dance someone snarls in irritation.
explanation.definitionFit: Vexation or mortification at having failed.

clue.text: Staff may have this to keep wine in

definitions.text: Staff may have this to keep wine in

parts.words: Staff may have this to keep wine in
parts.note: a staff or pole can have a banner on it, and the resulting phrase is a large vessel for wine

explanation.definitionFit: A large bottle or jug with a handle and spout, used for wine.

clue.text: Habitual criminal, big in Nigeria

parts.note: an old lag is a habitual offender
OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize

explanation.surface: A serial offender is a major figure in a West African country.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest city and former capital of the West African republic.

clue.text: Point of departure one waited for

parts.note: go means leave or depart
a dot is a point

explanation.surface: Someone was expected at the starting place.
explanation.walkthrough: The figure never arrives in Beckett's play Waiting for ...
explanation.definitionFit: The absent character in Beckett's play whom two tramps await in vain.

clue.text: "Smooth as monumental " (Othello)

parts.note: the solver completes Othello's line about Desdemona's skin, the missing word naming a pale stone used for tomb effigies

explanation.definitionFit: A fine white translucent stone carved for funeral monuments, which Othello compares to Desdemona's skin.

clue.text: Fruit eaten before the autumn in America

definitions.text: eaten before the autumn in America
definitions.meaning: Americans call autumn the fall, so this is the fruit Eve ate before the Fall of Man

explanation.definitionFit: A common orchard fruit, traditionally the one Eve ate before the Fall.

clue.text: Film sponsor

definitions.meaning: a man who stands sponsor for a child at baptism

explanation.definitionFit: The title of the Mafia epic and the man who vouches for a child at christening.

clue.text: Beat the seeds?

definitions.meaning: a regular throb of the heart in the arteries
edible seeds of legumes such as lentils and beans

explanation.definitionFit: A heartbeat throb; also the collective term for lentils, peas and beans.

clue.text: Fruit given to girl for flavouring

parts.note: a nut is botanically a fruit
Meg is a girl's name, short for Margaret

explanation.surface: Something given to a young woman to season food.
explanation.definitionFit: A spice grated from the seed of a tropical tree, used in cooking.

clue.text: After death, Reade's letters inspired affection

parts.note: the end is death

indicators.note: letters says the name's letters are taken and rearranged

parts.note: Charles Reade, the Victorian novelist, as written

explanation.surface: Once the novelist Reade had died, his correspondence won people's love.
explanation.definitionFit: To be made dear or beloved, winning someone's fondness.
